- Absence of respiratory distress/stridor/oropharyngeal swelling — makes anaphylaxis or upper airway obstruction unlikely, preserving cough as possible lower-airway mucosal involvement  

[GAPS]  
- Exact extent of skin detachment (% BSA) — required for SJS vs. TEN classification and SCORTEN scoring  
- Full mucosal exam results (ocular, oral, genital) — needed to confirm ≥2 mucosal sites (SJS criterion) and assess severity  
- Comprehensive medication history (especially sulfonamides, anticonvulsants, allopurinol, NSAIDs, antibiotics within prior 30 days) — essential to identify culprit drug  
- Absolute eosinophil count and serum IgE — may support drug hypersensitivity mechanism but are not diagnostic  
- O2 saturation and pulmonary imaging — to evaluate for bronchial mucosal involvement contributing to cough  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Drug-induced Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis (SJS/TEN) spectrum disorder.
